Answer: D
Reason: The combination of a right-sided pleural effusion, right lung atelectasis/hypoplasia, and a prominent left second cardiac arc (suggesting an enlarged pulmonary artery or anomalous venous channel) is characteristic of Scimitar syndrome (partial anomalous pulmonary venous return), where the right lung is often hypoplastic and drains anomalously to the IVC.
